## Summary of findings

After reading every test file under `./tests/` individually (the initial `ripgrep` pass returned no results, so I fell back to `read_tool` / `find_by_name`), I grouped the duplicated helpers into 6 buckets and verified each by reading the source.

### Confirmed duplicates (true copies or near-copies)

| # | Helper | Files | Verdict |
|---|--------|-------|---------|
| 1 | `parseDynamicRoute` + `buildTargetUrl` | [features/routing/fixed.js#L4-L99](file:///home/teric/win/e/dev/bot/model_proxy_v3/tests/features/routing/fixed.js#L4-L99), [api/sdk/integration.js#L49-L147](file:///home/teric/win/e/dev/bot/model_proxy_v3/tests/api/sdk/integration.js#L49-L147) + 2 more in-file copies in each | 5 copies; **drifted** (different `targetPathEndIndex` defaults, different comment ids) — not byte-identical |
| 2 | Bash `test_endpoint` curl/jq wrapper | 8+ shell scripts across `tests/providers/{claude,gemini}/*.sh` and `tests/infra/version.sh` | Two variants (PASS/FAIL with `.id`, PASS/FAIL with `grep data:`) — functionally identical |
| 3 | Auth-header builders in fetch() | [providers/gemini/sdk/openai-compatible.js](file:///home/teric/win/e/dev/bot/model_proxy_v3/tests/providers/gemini/sdk/openai-compatible.js), [native.js](file:///home/teric/win/e/dev/bot/model_proxy_v3/tests/providers/gemini/sdk/native.js), [simple.js](file:///home/teric/win/e/dev/bot/model_proxy_v3/tests/providers/gemini/sdk/simple.js), [api.js](file:///home/teric/win/e/dev/bot/model_proxy_v3/tests/providers/gemini/sdk/api.js) | Same scaffolding, different header names (`Authorization` / `x-goog-api-key` / `x-api-key`) and placeholder strings |
| 4 | `gemini -y -m "$model" -p "$prompt"` CLI loop | [providers/claude/models.sh](file:///home/teric/win/e/dev/bot/model_proxy_v3/tests/providers/claude/models.sh), [providers/gemini/cli.sh](file:///home/teric/win/e/dev/bot/model_proxy_v3/tests/providers/gemini/cli.sh), [providers/gemini/models.sh](file:///home/teric/win/e/dev/bot/model_proxy_v3/tests/providers/gemini/models.sh) | **Byte-identical** structure |
| 5 | SSE `getReader` loop | [providers/gemini/sdk/api.js#L226-L267](file:///home/teric/win/e/dev/bot/model_proxy_v3/tests/providers/gemini/sdk/api.js#L226-L267), [native.js#L75-L102](file:///home/teric/win/e/dev/bot/model_proxy_v3/tests/providers/gemini/sdk/native.js#L75-L102), [openai-compatible.js#L91-L114](file:///home/teric/win/e/dev/bot/model_proxy_v3/tests/providers/gemini/sdk/openai-compatible.js#L91-L114) | Native + openai-compatible are byte-identical; `api.js` adds per-chunk JSON parsing |
| 6 | `runTest` JS runner | [providers/gemini/sdk/api.js#L55-L66](file:///home/teric/win/e/dev/bot/model_proxy_v3/tests/providers/gemini/sdk/api.js#L55-L66), [providers/gemini/sdk/summary.js#L11-L19](file:///home/teric/win/e/dev/bot/model_proxy_v3/tests/providers/gemini/sdk/summary.js#L11-L19) | Functionally similar but **structurally different** (mutation vs return value) |

### NOT truly duplicates (left alone)

- `parseSimpleToml`, `getTokenizer`, `isNativeGeminiRequest` — each appears in only one file.
- The `proxy_config.toml` write/kill/restart boilerplate in shell tests — looks repetitive but each script writes a *different* fixture and runs *different* assertions, so the boilerplate is the test, not a helper.

### Recommended deduplication plan (priority order)

1. **Create `tests/helpers/lib.sh`** — bash `test_endpoint` + `test_sse` covering the curl/jq + SSE variants. Highest ROI, ~80 LoC removed across 8 scripts.
2. **Create `tests/helpers/routing.ts`** — single `parseDynamicRoute` + `buildTargetUrl`. Reconcile the drifted copies first.
3. **Create `tests/helpers/sse.js`** — `readSseStream(response, { onChunk })` with optional per-chunk JSON parsing.
4. **Create `tests/helpers/gemini-sdk.js`** — `geminiFetch({ authMode, ... })` to absorb the three SDK scripts' fetch boilerplate.
5. **Create `tests/helpers/cli.sh::run_gemini_cli_model`** — collapses the three identical `gemini -y -m` loops.
6. **Optional** — merge `runTest` / `assert` into `tests/helpers/runner.js` if more JS test files land.

The full report with file-by-file line ranges and the list of consumer files is in the artifact linked above.

To wait for the timer to fire, you must stop calling tools to end your turn.\n\nModes:\n1. **One-shot timer**: Set a timer for a specified duration that will notify you with your Prompt when it expires. You can control early termination behavior using TimerCondition:\n\n- 'never' (default): The timer will always fire after the specified duration, unless explicitly cancelled.\nUsage: Use when setting unconditional timers that should always fire after DurationSeconds, unless explicitly cancelled.\n- 'any': The timer will be cancelled early if ANY message from any sender is received before the duration.\nUsage: Useful when multiple background tasks are running and you want to wait for any update, but with some guarantee that you won't be idle forever in case they are all stuck.\n- <sender-id>: The timer will be cancelled early if a message is received from that specific sender ID.\nUsage: Use when you're waiting for an update from a specific subagent or task, but want to set some limit on how long to wait.\n\nNOTE: You cannot have multiple concurrently active timers that would early terminate on the same sender ID.\nFor example, if you already have a liveness timer set with \"any\", you cannot set another timer with \"any\" or any other condition.\nIf you already have a timer set with early termination on \"task-123\", you cannot set another timer with \"task-123\" or \"any\".\nYou should rely on the existing timer, or cancel and replace it if needed.\n\nExamples:\n\nScenario: User asks explicitly for a reminder in 10 minutes.\nArgs: DurationSeconds=600, Prompt=\"Remind the user\", TimerCondition=\"never\"\nComments: TimerCondition=\"never\" is appropriate since this timer is unrelated to other ongoing tasks.\n\nScenario: You just ran a command as \"task-123\". To wait for the timer to fire, you must stop calling tools to end your turn.\n\nModes:\n1. **One-shot timer**: Set a timer for a specified duration that will notify you with your Prompt when it expires. You can control early termination behavior using TimerCondition:\n\n- 'never' (default): The timer will always fire after the specified duration, unless explicitly cancelled.\nUsage: Use when setting unconditional timers that should always fire after DurationSeconds, unless explicitly cancelled.\n- 'any': The timer will be cancelled early if ANY message from any sender is received before the duration.\nUsage: Useful when multiple background tasks are running and you want to wait for any update, but with some guarantee that you won't be idle forever in case they are all stuck.\n- <sender-id>: The timer will be cancelled early if a message is received from that specific sender ID.\nUsage: Use when you're waiting for an update from a specific subagent or task, but want to set some limit on how long to wait.\n\nNOTE: You cannot have multiple concurrently active timers that would early terminate on the same sender ID.\nFor example, if you already have a liveness timer set with \"any\", you cannot set another timer with \"any\" or any other condition.\nIf you already have a timer set with early termination on \"task-123\", you cannot set another timer with \"task-123\" or \"any\".\nYou should rely on the existing timer, or cancel and replace it if needed.\n\nExamples:\n\nScenario: User asks explicitly for a reminder in 10 minutes.\nArgs: DurationSeconds=600, Prompt=\"Remind the user\", TimerCondition=\"never\"\nComments: TimerCondition=\"never\" is appropriate since this timer is unrelated to other ongoing tasks.\n\nScenario: You just ran a command as \"task-123\". You already set a notification on it for 5 minutes, and it just notified you that it's still running. After checking the output, you want to set a new reminder to check on it in 10 minutes if it still hasn't finished.\nArgs: DurationSeconds=600, Prompt=\"Check on the command status\", TimerCondition=\"task-123\"\nComments: TimerCondition=\"task-123\" is appropriate since the timer is not needed if the command finishes ahead of time.\n\nScenario: You just spawned 10 subagents, and you want to check in on progress after 5 minutes if you haven't heard back from any of them.\nArgs: DurationSeconds=300, Prompt=\"Check in on the subagents' progress\", TimerCondition=\"any\"\nComments: TimerCondition=\"any\" is appropriate since you are not waiting for any specific subagent.\n\nScenario: You are running a command that you're sure will terminate, and you want to wait for it to finish.\nArgs: N/A\nComments: A timer is not needed at all in this scenario and will wastefully generate extra messages. Each time the cron triggers, a notification with your Prompt is sent. The cron runs as a background task. Optionally set MaxIterations to limit the number of triggers.\n\nExamples:\n- Poll deployment status every 5 minutes: CronExpression=\"*/5 * * * *\", Prompt=\"Check deployment status and report progress\"\n- Run a health check every hour, up to 3 times: CronExpression=\"0 * * * *\", MaxIterations=3, Prompt=\"Run the health check script and report results\"\n\nGeneral Reminders:\n- You must specify exactly one of DurationSeconds or CronExpression.\n- Always provide a Prompt describing what the notification should say.\n- Never run a background 'sleep' command to set a timer, use this tool instead.\n- To cancel a running timer or cron schedule, use the manage_task tool with the task ID returned by this tool.","name":"schedule","parametersJsonSchema":{"$schema":"https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema","additionalProperties":false,"properties":{"CronExpression":{"description":"A standard cron expression (5 fields: minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week). To wait for the timer to fire, you must stop calling tools to end your turn.\n\nModes:\n1. **One-shot timer**: Set a timer for a specified duration that will notify you with your Prompt when it expires. You can control early termination behavior using TimerCondition:\n\n- 'never' (default): The timer will always fire after the specified duration, unless explicitly cancelled.\nUsage: Use when setting unconditional timers that should always fire after DurationSeconds, unless explicitly cancelled.\n- 'any': The timer will be cancelled early if ANY message from any sender is received before the duration.\nUsage: Useful when multiple background tasks are running and you want to wait for any update, but with some guarantee that you won't be idle forever in case they are all stuck.\n- <sender-id>: The timer will be cancelled early if a message is received from that specific sender ID.\nUsage: Use when you're waiting for an update from a specific subagent or task, but want to set some limit on how long to wait.\n\nNOTE: You cannot have multiple concurrently active timers that would early terminate on the same sender ID.\nFor example, if you already have a liveness timer set with \"any\", you cannot set another timer with \"any\" or any other condition.\nIf you already have a timer set with early termination on \"task-123\", you cannot set another timer with \"task-123\" or \"any\".\nYou should rely on the existing timer, or cancel and replace it if needed.\n\nExamples:\n\nScenario: User asks explicitly for a reminder in 10 minutes.\nArgs: DurationSeconds=600, Prompt=\"Remind the user\", TimerCondition=\"never\"\nComments: TimerCondition=\"never\" is appropriate since this timer is unrelated to other ongoing tasks.\n\nScenario: You just ran a command as \"task-123\". You already set a notification on it for 5 minutes, and it just notified you that it's still running. After checking the output, you want to set a new reminder to check on it in 10 minutes if it still hasn't finished.\nArgs: DurationSeconds=600, Prompt=\"Check on the command status\", TimerCondition=\"task-123\"\nComments: TimerCondition=\"task-123\" is appropriate since the timer is not needed if the command finishes ahead of time.\n\nScenario: You just spawned 10 subagents, and you want to check in on progress after 5 minutes if you haven't heard back from any of them.\nArgs: DurationSeconds=300, Prompt=\"Check in on the subagents' progress\", TimerCondition=\"any\"\nComments: TimerCondition=\"any\" is appropriate since you are not waiting for any specific subagent.\n\nScenario: You are running a command that you're sure will terminate, and you want to wait for it to finish.\nArgs: N/A\nComments: A timer is not needed at all in this scenario and will wastefully generate extra messages. Stop calling tools to end your turn instead.\n\n2. **Recurring cron**: Set CronExpression to a standard 5-field cron expression (e.g., '*/5 * * * *' for every 5 minutes). Each time the cron triggers, a notification with your Prompt is sent. The cron runs as a background task. Optionally set MaxIterations to limit the number of triggers.\n\nExamples:\n- Poll deployment status every 5 minutes: CronExpression=\"*/5 * * * *\", Prompt=\"Check deployment status and report progress\"\n- Run a health check every hour, up to 3 times: CronExpression=\"0 * * * *\", MaxIterations=3, Prompt=\"Run the health check script and report results\"\n\nGeneral Reminders:\n- You must specify exactly one of DurationSeconds or CronExpression.\n- Always provide a Prompt describing what the notification should say.\n- Never run a background 'sleep' command to set a timer, use this tool instead.\n- To cancel a running timer or cron schedule, use the manage_task tool with the task ID returned by this tool.","name":"schedule","parametersJsonSchema":{"$schema":"https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema","additionalProperties":false,"properties":{"CronExpression":{"description":"A standard cron expression (5 fields: minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week). To wait for the timer to fire, you must stop calling tools to end your turn.\n\nModes:\n1. **One-shot timer**: Set a timer for a specified duration that will notify you with your Prompt when it expires. To wait for the timer to fire, you must stop calling tools to end your turn.\n\nModes:\n1. **One-shot timer**: Set a timer for a specified duration that will notify you with your Prompt when it expires. You can control early termination behavior using TimerCondition:\n\n- 'never' (default): The timer will always fire after the specified duration, unless explicitly cancelled.\nUsage: Use when setting unconditional timers that should always fire after DurationSeconds, unless explicitly cancelled.\n- 'any': The timer will be cancelled early if ANY message from any sender is received before the duration.\nUsage: Useful when multiple background tasks are running and you want to wait for any update, but with some guarantee that you won't be idle forever in case they are all stuck.\n- <sender-id>: The timer will be cancelled early if a message is received from that specific sender ID.\nUsage: Use when you're waiting for an update from a specific subagent or task, but want to set some limit on how long to wait.\n\nNOTE: You cannot have multiple concurrently active timers that would early terminate on the same sender ID.\nFor example, if you already have a liveness timer set with \"any\", you cannot set another timer with \"any\" or any other condition.\nIf you already have a timer set with early termination on \"task-123\", you cannot set another timer with \"task-123\" or \"any\".\nYou should rely on the existing timer, or cancel and replace it if needed.\n\nExamples:\n\nScenario: User asks explicitly for a reminder in 10 minutes.\nArgs: DurationSeconds=600, Prompt=\"Remind the user\", TimerCondition=\"never\"\nComments: TimerCondition=\"never\" is appropriate since this timer is unrelated to other ongoing tasks.\n\nScenario: You just ran a command as \"task-123\". You already set a notification on it for 5 minutes, and it just notified you that it's still running. After checking the output, you want to set a new reminder to check on it in 10 minutes if it still hasn't finished.\nArgs: DurationSeconds=600, Prompt=\"Check on the command status\", TimerCondition=\"task-123\"\nComments: TimerCondition=\"task-123\" is appropriate since the timer is not needed if the command finishes ahead of time.\n\nScenario: You just spawned 10 subagents, and you want to check in on progress after 5 minutes if you haven't heard back from any of them.\nArgs: DurationSeconds=300, Prompt=\"Check in on the subagents' progress\", TimerCondition=\"any\"\nComments: TimerCondition=\"any\" is appropriate since you are not waiting for any specific subagent.\n\nScenario: You are running a command that you're sure will terminate, and you want to wait for it to finish.\nArgs: N/A\nComments: A timer is not needed at all in this scenario and will wastefully generate extra messages. Stop calling tools to end your turn instead.\n\n2. **Recurring cron**: Set CronExpression to a standard 5-field cron expression (e.g., '*/5 * * * *' for every 5 minutes). Each time the cron triggers, a notification with your Prompt is sent. The cron runs as a background task. Optionally set MaxIterations to limit the number of triggers.\n\nExamples:\n- Poll deployment status every 5 minutes: CronExpression=\"*/5 * * * *\", Prompt=\"Check deployment status and report progress\"\n- Run a health check every hour, up to 3 times: CronExpression=\"0 * * * *\", MaxIterations=3, Prompt=\"Run the health check script and report results\"\n\nGeneral Reminders:\n- You must specify exactly one of DurationSeconds or CronExpression.\n- Always provide a Prompt describing what the notification should say.\n- Never run a background 'sleep' command to set a timer, use this tool instead.\n- To cancel a running timer or cron schedule, use the manage_task tool with the task ID returned by this tool.","name":"schedule","parametersJsonSchema":{"$schema":"https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema","additionalProperties":false,"properties":{"CronExpression":{"description":"A standard cron expression (5 fields: minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week). You can control early termination behavior using TimerCondition:\n\n- 'never' (default): The timer will always fire after the specified duration, unless explicitly cancelled.\nUsage: Use when setting unconditional timers that should always fire after DurationSeconds, unless explicitly cancelled.\n- 'any': The timer will be cancelled early if ANY message from any sender is received before the duration.\nUsage: Useful when multiple background tasks are running and you want to wait for any update, but with some guarantee that you won't be idle forever in case they are all stuck.\n- <sender-id>: The timer will be cancelled early if a message is received from that specific sender ID.\nUsage: Use when you're waiting for an update from a specific subagent or task, but want to set some limit on how long to wait.\n\nNOTE: You cannot have multiple concurrently active timers that would early terminate on the same sender ID.\nFor example, if you already have a liveness timer set with \"any\", you cannot set another timer with \"any\" or any other condition.\nIf you already have a timer set with early termination on \"task-123\", you cannot set another timer with \"task-123\" or \"any\".\nYou should rely on the existing timer, or cancel and replace it if needed.\n\nExamples:\n\nScenario: User asks explicitly for a reminder in 10 minutes.\nArgs: DurationSeconds=600, Prompt=\"Remind the user\", TimerCondition=\"never\"\nComments: TimerCondition=\"never\" is appropriate since this timer is unrelated to other ongoing tasks.\n\nScenario: You just ran a command as \"task-123\". Each time the cron triggers, a notification with your Prompt is sent. The cron runs as a background task. Optionally set MaxIterations to limit the number of triggers.\n\nExamples:\n- Poll deployment status every 5 minutes: CronExpression=\"*/5 * * * *\", Prompt=\"Check deployment status and report progress\"\n- Run a health check every hour, up to 3 times: CronExpression=\"0 * * * *\", MaxIterations=3, Prompt=\"Run the health check script and report results\"\n\nGeneral Reminders:\n- You must specify exactly one of DurationSeconds or CronExpression.\n- Always provide a Prompt describing what the notification should say.\n- Never run a background 'sleep' command to set a timer, use this tool instead.\n- To cancel a running timer or cron schedule, use the manage_task tool with the task ID returned by this tool.","input_schema":{"type":"object","properties":{}}},{"name":"search_web","description":"Performs a web search for a given query. To wait for the timer to fire, you must stop calling tools to end your turn.\n\nModes:\n1. **One-shot timer**: Set a timer for a specified duration that will notify you with your Prompt when it expires. Expected format: /{protocol}{host}{path_prefix}/{model_id?}/{claude_endpoint}`);\\\\n  }\\\\n\\\\n  // First part is the protocol (http or https)\\\\n  const protocol = parts[0];\\\\n  if (protocol !== 'http' && protocol !== 'https') {\\\\n    throw new Error(`Invalid protocol: ${protocol}. Must be 'http' or 'https'`);\\\\n  }\\\\n\\\\n  // Second part is the host (e.g., api.groq.com)\\\\n  let host = parts[1];\\\\n\\\\n  // Find where the target API path ends and Claude endpoint begins\\\\n  // We look for known Claude endpoints: v1/models, v1/messages, v1/messages/count_tokens\\\\n  let targetPathEndIndex = -1;\\\\n  let claudeEndpointStartIndex = -1;\\\\n\\\\n  // Look for Claude endpoint patterns from the end\\\\n  for (let i = parts.length - 1; i >= 2; i--) {\\\\n    if (parts[i] === 'v1') {\\\\n      // Check if this is a Claude endpoint\\\\n      const nextPart = i + 1 < parts.length ? parts[i + 1] : null;\\\\n      const twoPartsAhead = i + 2 < parts.length ? parts[i + 2] : null;\\\\n\\\\n      if (nextPart === 'models' || nextPart === 'messages') {\\\\n        // Found a potential Claude endpoint\\\\n        targetPathEndIndex = i - 1;\\\\n        claudeEndpointStartIndex = i;\\\\n        break;\\\\n      }\\\\n\\\\n      if (nextPart === 'messages' && twoPartsAhead === 'count_tokens') {\\\\n        // Found token counting endpoint\\\\n        targetPathEndIndex = i - 1;\\\\n        claudeEndpointStartIndex = i;\\\\n        break;\\\\n      }\\\\n    }\\\\n  }\\\\n\\\\n  if (targetPathEndIndex === -1 || claudeEndpointStartIndex === -1) {\\\\n    throw new Error(`Could not locate Claude endpoint in URL: ${url}`);\\\\n  }\\\\n\\\\n  // Extract Claude endpoint path\\\\n  const claudeEndpointPath = parts.slice(claudeEndpointStartIndex).join('/');\\\\n\\\\n  // Determine if there's a model ID between target path and Claude endpoint\\\\n  let modelId = undefined;\\\\n  const betweenParts = parts.slice(targetPathEndIndex + 1, claudeEndpointStartIndex);\\\\n  if (betweenParts.length === 1) {\\\\n    // Likely a model ID\\\\n    modelId = betweenParts[0];\\\\n  } else if (betweenParts.length > 1) {\\\\n    // This might be part of the target path, adjust accordingly\\\\n    targetPathEndIndex = claudeEndpointStartIndex - 1;\\\\n    modelId = undefined;\\\\n\\\\n    // Recalculate\\\\n    const newTargetPathPrefix = parts.slice(2, targetPathEndIndex + 1).join('/');\\\\n    throw new Error(`Unclear URL structure. Between target path '${newTargetPathPrefix}' and Claude endpoint '${claudeEndpointPath}' found: ${betweenParts.join('/')}`);\\\\n  } else if (betweenParts.length === 0) {\\\\n    // Check if the last targetPathEndIndex + 1);\\\\n    if (targetPathParts.length > 0) {\\\\n      const lastPart = targetPathParts[targetPathParts.length - 1];\\\\n      // Check if last part looks like a model ID (not a common API path segment)\\\\n      const commonPathSegments = ['v1', 'v2', 'models', 'messages', 'completions', 'chat', 'openai', 'api'];\\\\n      if (!commonPathSegments.includes(lastPart) &&\\\\n          !lastPart.includes('/') &&\\\\n          lastPart.length > 0) {\\\\n        // This might be a model ID, extract it\\\\n        modelId = lastPart;\\\\n        // Adjust target path prefix to exclude the model ID\\\\n        targetPathEndIndex = targetPathEndIndex - 1;\\\\n      }\\\\n    }\\\\n  }\\\\n\\\\n  // Recalculate target path prefix in case we adjusted for model ID\\\\n  const finalTargetPathPrefix = parts.slice(2, targetPathEndIndex + 1).join('/');\\\\n\\\\n  const targetConfig = {\\\\n    targetUrl: `${protocol}://${host}`,\\\\n    targetPathPrefix: finalTargetPathPrefix ? `/${finalTargetPathPrefix}` : '',\\\\n  };\\\\n\\\\n  return {\\\\n    targetConfig,\\\\n    claudeEndpoint: claudeEndpointPath,\\\\n    modelId,\\\\n  };\\\\n}\\\\n\\\\n// Test each case\\\\nfor (const testUrl of testCases) {\\\\n  console.log(`Testing: ${testUrl}`);\\\\n  try {\\\\n    const result = parseDynamicRoute(testUrl);\\\\n    console.log(`  Protocol: }\\\\n}\\\\n\\\"}\\n```\"}"}]},{"role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"call_read_tool_0","name":"read_tool","input":{"path":"/home/teric/win/e/dev/bot/model_proxy_v3/tests/features/thinking/boolean.js"}},{"type":"tool_use","id":"call_read_tool_1","name":"read_tool","input":{"path":"/home/teric/win/e/dev/bot/model_proxy_v3/tests/features/token-counting/js-tiktoken.js"}}]},{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"tool_result","tool_use_id":"call_read_tool_0","content":"{\"output\":\"Tool const trimmed = line.trim();\\\\n\\\\n    // Skip comments and empty lines\\\\n    if (trimmed.startsWith('#') || trimmed === '') continue;\\\\n\\\\n    // Section header\\\\n    if (trimmed.startsWith('[') && trimmed.endsWith(']')) {\\\\n      currentSection = trimmed.slice(1, -1);\\\\n      if (!result[currentSection]) {\\\\n        result[currentSection] = {};\\\\n      }\\\\n      continue;\\\\n    }\\\\n\\\\n    // Key-value pair\\\\n    const eqIndex = trimmed.indexOf('=');\\\\n    if (eqIndex > 0) {\\\\n      const key = trimmed.slice(0, eqIndex).trim();\\\\n      let -1);\\\\n      }\\\\n\\\\n      if (currentSection) {\\\\n        result[currentSection][key] = value;\\\\n      } else {\\\\n        result[key] = value;\\\\n      }\\\\n    }\\\\n  }\\\\n\\\\n  return result;\\\\n}\\\\n\\\\nconst parsed = parseSimpleToml(tomlContent);\\\\nconsole.log('\\\\\\\\nParsed config:');\\\\nconsole.log(JSON.stringify(parsed, null, 2));\\\\n\\\\n// Test model }\\\\n}\\\"}\\n```\"}"},{"type":"tool_result","tool_use_id":"call_read_tool_1","content":"{\"output\":\"Tool response for read_tool:\\n```json\\n{\\\"result\\\": \\\"/**\\\\n * Performance test for js-tiktoken token counting\\\\n * Run: npx tsx tests/test_local_token_counting.ts\\\\n */\\\\n\\\\nimport { Tiktoken } from 'js-tiktoken/lite';\\\\nimport o200k_base from 'js-tiktoken/ranks/o200k_base';\\\\nimport cl100k_base from 'js-tiktoken/ranks/cl100k_base';\\\\nimport p50k_base from 'js-tiktoken/ranks/p50k_base';\\\\nimport p50k_edit from 'js-tiktoken/ranks/p50k_edit';\\\\nimport r50k_base from 'js-tiktoken/ranks/r50k_base';\\\\n\\\\n// Mapping of model names to encodings\\\\nconst ENCODINGS: Record<string, Uint8Array> = {\\\\n  'o200k_base': o200k_base,\\\\n  'cl100k_base': cl100k_base,\\\\n  'p50k_base': p50k_base,\\\\n  'p50k_edit': p50k_edit,\\\\n  'r50k_base': r50k_base,\\\\n};\\\\n\\\\ninterface TokenizerCache {\\\\n  tokenizer: Tiktoken | null;\\\\n  modelName: string;\\\\n}\\\\n\\\\nconst cache: TokenizerCache = {\\\\n  tokenizer: null,\\\\n  modelName: '',\\\\n};\\\\n\\\\nfunction getTokenizer(modelName: string = 'o200k_base'): Tiktoken {\\\\n  if (cache.tokenizer && cache.modelName === modelName) {\\\\n    return cache.tokenizer;\\\\n  }\\\\n\\\\n  const encoding = ENCODINGS[modelName] || o200k_base;\\\\n  cache.tokenizer = new Tiktoken(encoding);\\\\n  cache.modelName = modelName;\\\\n  return cache.tokenizer;\\\\n}\\\\n\\\\nfunction countTokens(text: string, modelName: string = 'o200k_base'): number {\\\\n  const tokenizer = getTokenizer(modelName);\\\\n  const tokens = tokenizer.encode(text);\\\\n  return tokens.length;\\\\n}\\\\n\\\\nfunction estimateTokenCount(text: string, charactersPerToken: number = 4): number {\\\\n  return Math.ceil(text.length / charactersPerToken);\\\\n}\\\\n\\\\n// Test data: various text types\\\\nconst testCases = [\\\\n  { name: 'Short English', text: 'Hello, world!' },\\\\n  { name: 'Medium English', text: 'The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog. This is a sample sentence for testing tokenization.' },\\\\n  { name: 'Long English', text: `\\\\n    Artificial intelligence (AI) has rapidly transformed from a speculative concept to a practical reality that impacts nearly every aspect of modern life.\\\\n    From healthcare diagnostics to autonomous vehicles, from recommendation algorithms to natural language processing, AI systems are increasingly embedded in our daily experiences.\\\\n    Machine learning, a subset of AI, enables computers to learn patterns from data without being explicitly programmed for every possible scenario.\\\\n    Deep learning, with its neural networks inspired by the human brain, has achieved remarkable breakthroughs in image recognition, speech synthesis, and strategic games.\\\\n    However, AI also raises important questions about bias, transparency, job displacement, and the ethical use of powerful computational systems.\\\\n    As we continue to develop more sophisticated AI technologies, it becomes crucial to ensure these systems are designed and deployed responsibly.\\\\n    Researchers, policymakers, and industry leaders must collaborate to establish guidelines that maximize benefits while minimizing potential harms.\\\\n    The future of AI holds tremendous promise for solving complex global challenges, from climate change to disease prevention, if we approach its development thoughtfully.\\\\n  `.trim() },\\\\n  { name: 'Chinese', text: '\\\\u4eba\\\\u5de5\\\\u667a\\\\u80fd\\\\u6b63\\\\u5728\\\\u5feb\\\\u901f\\\\u6539\\\\u53d8\\\\u6211\\\\u4eec\\\\u7684\\\\u4e16\\\\u754c\\\\uff0c\\\\u4ece\\\\u533b\\\\u7597\\\\u4fdd\\\\u5065\\\\u5230\\\\u81ea\\\\u52a8\\\\u9a7e\\\\u9a76\\\\u6c7d\\\\u8f66\\\\uff0c\\\\u4ece\\\\u63a8\\\\u8350\\\\u7cfb\\\\u7edf\\\\u5230\\\\u81ea\\\\u7136\\\\u8bed\\\\u8a00\\\\u5904\\\\u7406\\\\u3002' },\\\\n  { name: 'Code - TypeScript', text: `\\\\n    function calculateFactorial(n: number): number {\\\\n      if (n <= 1) return 1;\\\\n      return n * calculateFactorial(n - 1);\\\\n    }\\\\n\\\\n    interface User {\\\\n      id: number;\\\\n      name: string;\\\\n      email: string;\\\\n    }\\\\n\\\\n    class UserService {\\\\n      private users: User[] = [];\\\\n\\\\n      async createUser(user: Omit<User, 'id'>): Promise<User> {\\\\n        const newUser = { ...user, id: Date.now() };\\\\n        this.users.push(newUser);\\\\n        return newUser;\\\\n      }\\\\n    }\\\\n  `.trim() },\\\\n  { name: 'JSON Data', text: JSON.stringify({ users: [{ id: 1, name: 'Alice' }, { id: 2, name: 'Bob' }] }, null, 2) },\\\\n  { name: 'System Prompt', text: 'You are a helpful, harmless, and honest AI assistant. You always think step by step before answering. Your responses should be clear, concise, and accurate.' },\\\\n];\\\\n\\\\nconst models = ['o200k_base', 'cl100k_base'];\\\\n\\\\ninterface BenchmarkResult {\\\\n  encoding: string;\\\\n  testCase: string;\\\\n  textLength: number;\\\\n  tokenCount: number;\\\\n  timeMs: number;\\\\n}\\\\n\\\\nconst results: BenchmarkResult[] = [];\\\\n\\\\nasync function runBenchmarks() {\\\\n  console.log('=== js-tiktoken Performance Test ===\\\\\\\\n');\\\\n\\\\n  for (const model of models) {\\\\n    console.log(`Testing encoding: ${model}\\\\\\\\n`);\\\\n    console.log('| Test Case | Chars | Tokens | Est. Tokens | Error % | Time (ms) |');\\\\n    console.log('|-----------|-------|--------|-------------|---------|----------|');\\\\n\\\\n    for (const testCase of testCases) {\\\\n      const text = testCase.text;\\\\n      const textLength = text.length;\\\\n\\\\n      // Warm up\\\\n      countTokens(text.slice(0, 100), model);\\\\n\\\\n      // Benchmark\\\\n      const iterations = 1000;\\\\n      const start = performance.now();\\\\n      for (let i = 0; i < iterations; i++) {\\\\n        countTokens(text, model);\\\\n      }\\\\n      const end = performance.now();\\\\n\\\\n      const tokenCount = countTokens(text, model);\\\\n      const estimatedTokens = estimateTokenCount(text);\\\\n      const errorPercent = ((tokenCount - estimatedTokens) / estimatedTokens * 100).toFixed(1);\\\\n      const timeMs = ((end - start) / iterations).toFixed(3);\\\\n\\\\n      console.log(`| ${testCase.name} | ${textLength} | ${tokenCount} | ${estimatedTokens} | ${errorPercent}% | ${timeMs} |`);\\\\n\\\\n      results.push({\\\\n        encoding: model,\\\\n        testCase: testCase.name,\\\\n        textLength,\\\\n        tokenCount,\\\\n        timeMs: parseFloat(timeMs),\\\\n      });\\\\n    }\\\\n    console.log('');\\\\n  }\\\\n\\\\n  // Summary\\\\n  console.log('=== Summary ===\\\\\\\\n');\\\\n  console.log('Average time per token (lower is better):\\\\\\\\n');\\\\n\\\\n  for (const model of models) {\\\\n    const modelResults = results.filter(r => r.encoding === model);\\\\n    const totalTime = modelResults.reduce((sum, r) => sum + r.timeMs, 0);\\\\n    const totalTokens = modelResults.reduce((sum, r) => sum + r.tokenCount, 0);\\\\n    const avgTimePerToken = (totalTime / totalTokens * 1000).toFixed(4);\\\\n\\\\n    console.log(`${model}: ${avgTimePerToken} ms per token`);\\\\n  }\\\\n\\\\n  // Token density analysis\\\\n  console.log('\\\\\\\\nToken density (tokens per character):\\\\\\\\n');\\\\n  for (const model of models) {\\\\n    const modelResults = results.filter(r => r.encoding === model);\\\\n    const avgDensity = modelResults.reduce((sum, r) => sum + r.tokenCount / r.textLength, 0) / modelResults.length;\\\\n    console.log(`${model}: ${(avgDensity * 100).toFixed(1)}% (1 token per ${(1 / avgDensity).toFixed(1)} chars)`);\\\\n  }\\\\n\\\\n  console.log('\\\\\\\\n=== Test Complete Expected format: /{protocol}{host}{path_prefix}/{model_id?}/{claude_endpoint}`);\\\\n  }\\\\n\\\\n  // First part is the protocol (http or https)\\\\n  const protocol = parts[0];\\\\n  if (protocol !== 'http' && protocol !== 'https') {\\\\n    throw new Error(`Invalid protocol: ${protocol}. Must be 'http' or 'https'`);\\\\n  }\\\\n\\\\n  // Second part is the host (e.g., api.groq.com)\\\\n  let host = parts[1];\\\\n\\\\n  // Find where the target API path ends and Claude endpoint begins\\\\n  // We look for known Claude endpoints: v1/models, v1/messages, v1/messages/count_tokens\\\\n  let targetPathEndIndex = -1;\\\\n  let claudeEndpointStartIndex = -1;\\\\n\\\\n  // Look for Claude endpoint patterns from the end\\\\n  for (let i = parts.length - 1; i >= 2; i--) {\\\\n    if (parts[i] === 'v1') {\\\\n      // Check if this is a Claude endpoint\\\\n      const nextPart = i + 1 < parts.length ? parts[i + 1] : null;\\\\n      const twoPartsAhead = i + 2 < parts.length ? parts[i + 2] : null;\\\\n\\\\n      if (nextPart === 'models' || nextPart === 'messages') {\\\\n        // Found a potential Claude endpoint\\\\n        targetPathEndIndex = i - 1;\\\\n        claudeEndpointStartIndex = i;\\\\n        break;\\\\n      }\\\\n\\\\n      if (nextPart === 'messages' && twoPartsAhead === 'count_tokens') {\\\\n        // Found token counting endpoint\\\\n        targetPathEndIndex = i - 1;\\\\n        claudeEndpointStartIndex = i;\\\\n        break;\\\\n      }\\\\n    }\\\\n  }\\\\n\\\\n  if (targetPathEndIndex === -1 || claudeEndpointStartIndex === -1) {\\\\n    throw new Error(`Could not locate Claude endpoint in URL: ${url}`);\\\\n  }\\\\n\\\\n  // Extract Claude endpoint path\\\\n  const claudeEndpointPath = parts.slice(claudeEndpointStartIndex).join('/');\\\\n\\\\n  // Determine if there's a model ID between target path and Claude endpoint\\\\n  let modelId = undefined;\\\\n  const betweenParts = parts.slice(targetPathEndIndex + 1, claudeEndpointStartIndex);\\\\n  if (betweenParts.length === 1) {\\\\n    // Likely a model ID\\\\n    modelId = betweenParts[0];\\\\n  } else if (betweenParts.length > 1) {\\\\n    // This might be part of the target path, adjust accordingly\\\\n    targetPathEndIndex = claudeEndpointStartIndex - 1;\\\\n    modelId = undefined;\\\\n\\\\n    // Recalculate\\\\n    const newTargetPathPrefix = parts.slice(2, targetPathEndIndex + 1).join('/');\\\\n    throw new Error(`Unclear URL structure. common API path segment)\\\\n      const commonPathSegments = ['v1', 'v2', 'models', 'messages', 'completions', 'chat', 'openai', 'api'];\\\\n      if (!commonPathSegments.includes(lastPart) &&\\\\n          !lastPart.includes('/') &&\\\\n          lastPart.length > 0) {\\\\n        // This might be a model ID, extract it\\\\n        modelId = lastPart;\\\\n        // Adjust target path prefix to exclude the model ID\\\\n        targetPathEndIndex = targetPathEndIndex - 1;\\\\n      }\\\\n    }\\\\n  }\\\\n\\\\n  // Recalculate target path prefix in case we adjusted for model ID\\\\n  const finalTargetPathPrefix = parts.slice(2, targetPathEndIndex + 1).join('/');\\\\n\\\\n  const targetConfig = {\\\\n    targetUrl: `${protocol}://${host}`,\\\\n    targetPathPrefix: finalTargetPathPrefix ? `/${finalTargetPathPrefix}` : '',\\\\n  };\\\\n\\\\n  return {\\\\n    targetConfig,\\\\n    claudeEndpoint: claudeEndpointPath,\\\\n    modelId,\\\\n  };\\\\n}\\\\n\\\\n// Test each case\\\\nfor 'o200k_base': o200k_base,\\\\n  'cl100k_base': cl100k_base,\\\\n  'p50k_base': p50k_base,\\\\n  'p50k_edit': p50k_edit,\\\\n  'r50k_base': r50k_base,\\\\n};\\\\n\\\\ninterface TokenizerCache {\\\\n  tokenizer: Tiktoken | null;\\\\n  modelName: string;\\\\n}\\\\n\\\\nconst cache: TokenizerCache = {\\\\n  tokenizer: null,\\\\n  modelName: '',\\\\n};\\\\n\\\\nfunction getTokenizer(modelName: string = 'o200k_base'): Tiktoken {\\\\n  if (cache.tokenizer && cache.modelName === modelName) {\\\\n    return cache.tokenizer;\\\\n  }\\\\n\\\\n  const encoding = ENCODINGS[modelName] || o200k_base;\\\\n  cache.tokenizer = new Tiktoken(encoding);\\\\n  cache.modelName = modelName;\\\\n  return cache.tokenizer;\\\\n}\\\\n\\\\nfunction countTokens(text: string, modelName: string = 'o200k_base'): number {\\\\n  const tokenizer = getTokenizer(modelName);\\\\n  const tokens = tokenizer.encode(text);\\\\n  return tokens.length;\\\\n}\\\\n\\\\nfunction estimateTokenCount(text: string, charactersPerToken: TypeScript', text: `\\\\n    function calculateFactorial(n: number): number {\\\\n      if (n <= 1) return 1;\\\\n      return n * calculateFactorial(n - 1);\\\\n    }\\\\n\\\\n    interface User {\\\\n      id: number;\\\\n      name: string;\\\\n      email: string;\\\\n    }\\\\n\\\\n    class UserService {\\\\n      private users: User[] = [];\\\\n\\\\n      async createUser(user: Omit<User, 'id'>): Promise<User> {\\\\n        const newUser = { ...user, id: Date.now() };\\\\n        this.users.push(newUser);\\\\n        return newUser;\\\\n      }\\\\n    }\\\\n  `.trim() },\\\\n  { name: 'JSON Data', text: JSON.stringify({ users: [{ id: 1, name: 'Alice' }, { id: 2, name: 'Bob' }] }, null, 2) },\\\\n  { name: 'System Prompt', text: 'You are a helpful, harmless, and honest AI assistant. Tokens | Error % | Time (ms) |');\\\\n    console.log('|-----------|-------|--------|-------------|---------|----------|');\\\\n\\\\n    for (const testCase of testCases) {\\\\n      const text =      const start = performance.now();\\\\n      for (let i = 0; i < iterations; i++) {\\\\n        countTokens(text, model);\\\\n      }\\\\n      const end = performance.now();\\\\n\\\\n      const console.log(`${model}: ${avgTimePerToken} ms per token`);\\\\n  }\\\\n\\\\n  // Token density analysis\\\\n  console.log('\\\\\\\\nToken density (tokens per character):\\\\\\\\n');\\\\n  for (const 'p50k_base': p50k_base,\\n  'p50k_edit': p50k_edit,\\n  'r50k_base': r50k_base,\\n};\\n\\ninterface TokenizerCache {\\n  tokenizer: Tiktoken | null;\\n  modelName: string;\\n}\\n\\nconst cache: 'js-tiktoken/ranks/p50k_edit';\\\\nimport r50k_base from 'js-tiktoken/ranks/r50k_base';\\\\n\\\\n// Mapping of model names to encodings\\\\nconst ENCODINGS: Record<string, Uint8Array> = {\\\\n  'o200k_base': o200k_base,\\\\n  'cl100k_base': cl100k_base,\\\\n  'p50k_base': p50k_base,\\\\n  'p50k_edit': p50k_edit,\\\\n  'r50k_base': r50k_base,\\\\n};\\\\n\\\\ninterface TokenizerCache {\\\\n  tokenizer: Tiktoken | null;\\\\n  modelName: string;\\\\n}\\\\n\\\\nconst cache: TokenizerCache = {\\\\n  tokenizer: null,\\\\n  modelName: '',\\\\n};\\\\n\\\\nfunction getTokenizer(modelName: string = 'o200k_base'): Tiktoken {\\\\n  if (cache.tokenizer && cache.modelName === modelName) {\\\\n    return cache.tokenizer;\\\\n  }\\\\n\\\\n  const encoding = ENCODINGS[modelName] || o200k_base;\\\\n  cache.tokenizer = new Tiktoken(encoding);\\\\n  cache.modelName = modelName;\\\\n  return cache.tokenizer;\\\\n}\\\\n\\\\nfunction countTokens(text: string, modelName: string = 'o200k_base'): number {\\\\n  const tokenizer = getTokenizer(modelName);\\\\n  const tokens = tokenizer.encode(text);\\\\n  return tokens.length;\\\\n}\\\\n\\\\nfunction estimateTokenCount(text: string, charactersPerToken: TypeScript', text: `\\\\n    function calculateFactorial(n: number): number {\\\\n      if (n <= 1) return 1;\\\\n      return n * calculateFactorial(n - 1);\\\\n    }\\\\n\\\\n    interface User {\\\\n      id: number;\\\\n      name: string;\\\\n      email: string;\\\\n    }\\\\n\\\\n    class UserService {\\\\n      private users: User[] = [];\\\\n\\\\n      async createUser(user: Omit<User, 'id'>): Promise<User> {\\\\n        const newUser = { ...user, id: Date.now() };\\\\n        this.users.push(newUser);\\\\n        return newUser;\\\\n      }\\\\n    }\\\\n  `.trim() },\\\\n  { name: 'JSON Data', text: JSON.stringify({ users: [{ id: 1, name: 'Alice' }, { id: 2, name: 'Bob' }] }, null, 2) },\\\\n  { name: 'System Prompt', text: 'You are a helpful, harmless, and honest AI assistant. You always think step by step before answering. Your responses should be clear, concise, and accurate.' },\\\\n];\\\\n\\\\nconst models = ['o200k_base', 'cl100k_base'];\\\\n\\\\ninterface BenchmarkResult {\\\\n  encoding: string;\\\\n  testCase: string;\\\\n  textLength: number;\\\\n  tokenCount: number;\\\\n  timeMs: number;\\\\n}\\\\n\\\\nconst results: BenchmarkResult[] = [];\\\\n\\\\nasync function runBenchmarks() {\\\\n  console.log('=== js-tiktoken Performance Test ===\\\\\\\\n');\\\\n\\\\n  for (const model of models) {\\\\n    console.log(`Testing encoding: ${model}\\\\\\\\n`);\\\\n    console.log('| Test Case | Chars | Tokens | Est. Tokens | Error % | Time (ms) |');\\\\n    console.log('|-----------|-------|--------|-------------|---------|----------|');\\\\n\\\\n    for (const testCase of testCases) {\\\\n      const text = testCase.text;\\\\n      const textLength = text.length;\\\\n\\\\n      // Warm up\\\\n      countTokens(text.slice(0, 100), model);\\\\n\\\\n      // Benchmark\\\\n      const iterations = 1000;\\\\n      const start = performance.now();\\\\n      for (let i = 0; i < iterations; i++) {\\\\n        countTokens(text, model);\\\\n      }\\\\n      const end = performance.now();\\\\n\\\\n      const tokenCount = countTokens(text, model);\\\\n      const estimatedTokens = estimateTokenCount(text);\\\\n      const errorPercent = ((tokenCount - estimatedTokens) / estimatedTokens * better):\\\\\\\\n');\\\\n\\\\n  for (const model of models) {\\\\n    const modelResults = results.filter(r => r.encoding === model);\\\\n    const totalTime = modelResults.reduce((sum, r) => sum + Every line range cited below comes from that second pass.\n\n---\n\n## 1. `parseDynamicRoute` (JS re-implementations)\n\nThree JS files each define their **own** copy of `parseDynamicRoute` plus a `buildTargetUrl` companion:\n\n| File | Lines |\n|------|-------|\n| [features/routing/fixed.js](file:///home/teric/win/e/dev/bot/model_proxy_v3/tests/features/routing/fixed.js) | 4-99 (`parseDynamicRoute`) + 70-76 (`buildTargetUrl`) — and a second copy at 109-198 |\n| [api/sdk/integration.js](file:///home/teric/win/e/dev/bot/model_proxy_v3/tests/api/sdk/integration.js) | 49-138 (`parseDynamicRoute`) + 140-147 (`buildTargetUrl`) — and second/third copies at 156-245 and 252-336 |\n| (No other JS file) | only the routing/integration tests carry this helper |\n\n### Are they truly identical?\n\n**No — they have drifted.**\n\n- `fixed.js` (lines 4-99): parses `parts`, scans for Claude endpoint, extracts `modelId` from `betweenParts`, supports `[models.default]` style prefix detection; comments reference `src/utils/validation.ts:39-41`.\n- `integration.js` (lines 49-138): byte-for-byte equivalent in structure but uses slightly different comment text (`Simplified parseDynamicRoute logic`, `Wait, targetPathPrefix should be empty since we have modelId \"abc\"`). The `targetPathEndIndex = 1` hard-code in `integration.js` is **not** present in `fixed.js`.\n- The duplicate copies inside the same files (`integration.js` lines 156-245, 252-336; `fixed.js` lines 109-198) repeat the *same* function with only variable-name renames (`finalTargetPathPrefix` vs `targetPathPrefix`).\n\nThe duplication is real but the copies have **diverged in subtle ways** (different comment ids, different default-index values). Any refactor must reconcile these.\n\n**Recommendation:** extract to `tests/helpers/routing.ts` exporting `parseDynamicRoute` and `buildTargetUrl`. Replace the 5 inline copies with imports. ~250 LoC removed.\n\n---\n\n## 2. Bash `test_endpoint` wrapper (curl + jq)\n\nEvery shell test defines its own `test_endpoint` (or `test_sse`) helper. The bodies differ in three flavours:\n\n### Variant A: PASS / FAIL with jq `.id` check (most common)\n\n```\ntests/providers/claude/basic.sh         lines 12-25\ntests/providers/claude/models.sh        lines 12-25  (in 3 of the 5 inline scripts concatenated)\ntests/providers/claude/modes.sh         lines 21-34, 81-94  (same body re-declared twice)\ntests/providers/gemini/basic.sh         lines 12-25\ntests/providers/gemini/models.sh        lines 12-25\ntests/providers/gemini/modes.sh         lines 53-66\n```\n\nBody: `curl -s \"$url\" -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" -d \"$data\"` → `jq -e '.id'` → on success increment `((PASS++))`, on failure extract `.error.message // .message // \"Unknown error\"`.\n\n### Variant B: PASS / FAIL with `curl -N` + `grep -qE \"^(event:|data:)\"` for SSE\n\n```\ntests/providers/gemini/modes.sh         lines 39-51\ntests/providers/gemini/streaming.sh     lines 18-31  (test_endpoint) and lines 87-100 (test_sse)\n```\n\n### Variant C: PASS / FAIL with `curl -s -X POST` + grep for `\"id\"` / SSE lines\n\n```\ntests/providers/gemini/streaming.sh     lines 14-21, 99-110\ntests/infra/version.sh                  lines 8-12 (no PASS/FAIL counters, only a smoke test)\n```\n\n### Variant D: `gemini` CLI wrapper (no curl)\n\n```\ntests/providers/claude/models.sh        lines 21-37 (script 1)\ntests/providers/gemini/cli.sh           lines 19-36\ntests/providers/gemini/models.sh        lines 20-37\n```\n\nAll variants are **functionally identical** except for:\n- Variant B adds the `-N` flag for streaming.\n- Variant C uses `grep -qE \"^(event:|data:)\"` instead of `jq -e '.id'`.\n- The CLI variant does not call `curl` at all.\n\n**Recommendation:** create `tests/helpers/lib.sh` sourcing a single `test_endpoint` that takes a `--stream` flag, plus a `test_cli_model` companion. Replace the 8+ copies.\n\n---\n\n## 3. Auth-header builders (Node)\n\nThree Gemini SDK tests each open-code the same `Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY` block:\n\n| File | Lines |\n|------|-------|\n| [providers/gemini/sdk/openai-compatible.js](file:///home/teric/win/e/dev/bot/model_proxy_v3/tests/providers/gemini/sdk/openai-compatible.js) | 19, 73, 110 (Bearer) and 57 (`x-api-key`) |\n| [providers/gemini/sdk/native.js](file:///home/teric/win/e/dev/bot/model_proxy_v3/tests/providers/gemini/sdk/native.js) | 17, 53, 91 (`x-goog-api-key: YOUR_GEMINI_API_KEY`) |\n| [providers/gemini/sdk/simple.js](file:///home/teric/win/e/dev/bot/model_proxy_v3/tests/providers/gemini/sdk/simple.js) | 17 |\n\nThe header names differ (`Authorization` vs `x-goog-api-key` vs `x-api-key`), and the constant string literal differs (`YOUR_API_KEY` vs `YOUR_GEMINI_API_KEY`). The body literal `process.env.GEMINI_API_KEY || 'test-api-key'` appears only in [providers/gemini/sdk/api.js:7](file:///home/teric/win/e/dev/bot/model_proxy_v3/tests/providers/gemini/sdk/api.js#L7).\n\n**Are they truly identical?** No — the auth-header *name* and the *placeholder literal* differ per file, but the surrounding fetch/JSON/Content-Type scaffolding is the same. They cannot share an implementation without changing `summary.js`'s flow.\n\n**Recommendation:** pick one shape; either move `assert` + `runTest` into `tests/helpers/runner.js` and adopt it in `summary.js`, or rewrite `summary.js` to share `api.js`'s pattern.\n\n---\n\n## 7.
